description: We guess the name says it all, I guess?
summary:
Not Quite Mars? is an interactive tool that takes any point on the Moon and returns the Earth location with the matching terrain slope. We cleaned NASA LRO LOLA lunar elevation data and MODIS elevation data for Turkey’s Marmara region. We calculated slope at each point from its 12 nearest neighbors within 2.5 km, then built a clickable map that finds the best match.

The challenge asks for Earth locations that analog the permanent Moon base sites and Mars. Gravity can’t be reproduced on Earth, so we match terrain slope, one of the key environmental parameters. In our test, a lunar point with a slope of 0.016319° matched a Marmara location at 40.1167°N, 28.1579°E with a slope of 0.016323°, a 99.98% match.

This matters because missions can’t be tested on the Moon or Mars before launch. Realistic Earth analogs let teams test rovers, equipment and crew training sooner, more safely and at lower cost. The same method can extend to temperature, soil and Mars.
